Supporting multimodal inputs does not ensure
reliable task completion.

517 evaluation instances · 4 reasoning scenarios · 41.97% overall success

From multimodal inputs to physical reasoning

Can a model infer what to generate from incomplete, complementary multimodal evidence? We evaluate MiniMax-H3 with implicit prompts that leave task-relevant information unstated. Solving these tasks requires integrating observations and producing an appropriate visual outcome.

The evaluation spans spatial correspondence, acoustic disambiguation, decisions from observed dynamics, and audiovisual integration. Across 517 instances in 29 subcategories, the model achieves a sample-weighted human-evaluated success rate of 41.97%. Success measures whether the requested task is satisfied, rather than visual quality alone.

Four ways to reason from evidence

MSRMulti-view Spatial Reasoning

Establish cross-view correspondence and spatial consistency from multiple images and text.

200 instances · 10 subcategories

ADRAudio-based Disambiguation Reasoning

Resolve an ambiguous visual event using acoustic evidence, an image, and text.

146 instances · 6 subcategories

VDRVideo-based Decision Reasoning

Infer an appropriate continuation from observed dynamics in a prefix video and text.

100 instances · 8 subcategories

AVIRAudiovisual Integrated Reasoning

Ground audio evidence or spoken constraints in video continuation or editing.

71 instances · 5 subcategories

Overall success is weighted by the number of instances. Differences across scenarios are not controlled comparisons of input modalities.

When sound changes the visual interpretation

Audio-based disambiguation asks the model to infer a visual event from acoustic evidence, such as a cabinet opening or a typewriter in use.

One failure described in the manuscript: cat-meowing audio animates the dog while the cat remains inactive. Matching the sound to the correct visible entity remains challenging.

Evaluation protocol & scope

Task satisfaction, judged by people

Three experts independently judge generated outputs and cross-check their assessments. Multiple valid outputs are accepted when they satisfy the task.

Behavioral evidence, with limits

Generated outputs reveal task behavior; they do not directly expose internal reasoning. The four scenarios differ in task composition and should be interpreted within their respective settings.
